title: A selected model with ten years of rain history left an AGCD runoff deficit at 173 south-east Australian catchments in 2010-2021
abstract: We test whether a fixed rainfall-memory relation can explain both an annual runoff loss and its growth in wet years. We use published CAMELS-AUS v2.03 annual data at 173 south-east Australian catchments. Earlier held-out years select a regional rainfall window and penalty. The model allows 3, 5 or 10 years of rain history, a square and a current-rain interaction. Fits end in 1996. With AGCD rain, the selected model leaves a 2010-2021 mean residual of -40.1 mm/year, with a conditional 95% interval of -68.2 to -15.8. Memory changes the residual by -0.9 mm/year [-2.7, +0.7]. The normalized residual rain slope stays negative at -0.244 [-0.361, -0.060]. The nested historical test gives no clear prediction gain: -0.08% [-2.58%, +2.15%]. With SILO rain, selection chooses baseline and the late mean interval reaches zero. This limits a fixed rainfall-memory explanation for AGCD, not groundwater processes. Source dependence, climate extrapolation, negative predictions, short training and conditional intervals limit inference. Exact annual inputs, source rights, hashes, code, draws, predictions, audits and an offline repeat are included.

display.caption: Late mean runoff residual and normalized residual rain slope under baseline and selected memory relations. Intervals condition on fits and model selection. SILO shows the best forced memory candidate; its full selection chose baseline.
